units.title: Hierarchical task-network inference and plan existence

required_components.description: Define primitive, compound and goal tasks, operators, methods, constraint formulas and initial task networks.
required_components.success_condition: A reader can distinguish action executability from derivability through allowed methods.
required_components.failure_condition: A goal-satisfying action sequence is accepted without a permitted task decomposition.

required_components.description: Specify reduction, grounding, ordering and the solution relation with protected intermediate conditions.
required_components.success_condition: A complete derivation records each method application and validates the resulting primitive execution.
required_components.failure_condition: Subtasks are treated as independent while ordering or intermediate-state conditions are violated.

required_components.description: Supply the source's plan-existence and restriction results with their actual proofs.
required_components.success_condition: Retain differences between ordered methods and a totally ordered problem, variables and propositional instances, regularity and bounded-level mappings.
required_components.failure_condition: Finite world-state space or totally ordered individual methods is incorrectly treated as a general termination guarantee.

required_components.description: Explain the precise comparison with STRIPS-style state-goal planning.
required_components.success_condition: State what translations preserve and prove the selected expressivity separation with its representation assumptions.
required_components.failure_condition: HTN is described as only a search-speed trick or as equivalent to unrestricted general-purpose planning.

required_components.description: Work an executable decomposition and a method-relative failure; connect the result to practical task reasoning.
required_components.success_condition: The successful plan includes its derivation and every intermediate check; the failure identifies a missing method or violated constraint.
required_components.failure_condition: Failure of the available method set is declared physical impossibility or an unbounded search is called proof of no plan.
